page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Eadsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a 236 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities. The E4ads_v7 achieves top-tier results in single-core CPU performance via stress-ng, as well as single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-threaded scaling presents a clear tradeoff. Multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests falls into the average category, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only cached small blocks reaching 450.1 GB/sec and uncached large blocks reaching 46.8 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also align with average tier expectations.

With 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the E4ads_v7 is positioned as a memory-optimized instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallelization. It is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and single-threaded data processing tasks. Conversely, it is poorly suited for medium-sized large language model inference, where prompt processing speeds fall into the bottom 10%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of memory relative to its vCPU count, making it a resource-efficient choice for workloads constrained by memory capacity rather than raw multi-core compute power.
